title: The 3D Universe in a book
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-01007-7

Brian May and Derek Ward-Thompson discuss the dynamical world of modern astronomy, which is beautifully captured in their stereoscopic book, Islands in Infinity.

title: Carnot’s cycle in the making of thermodynamics
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-00994-x

Starting from the problem of steam engines, Sadi Carnot’s ideal cycle became a way to compare real processes with physical limits. Physicist and historian of the physical and mathematical sciences Raffaele Pisano traces how machines, diagrams, later theoretical reinterpretation and archival evidence turned an engineering problem into a durable thermodynamic law.

title: Taking the temperature of a cancer cell
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-01013-9

An article in Science Advances introduces a method for measuring the temperature inside living cells.

title: Tipping points in complex ecological systems
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-00987-w

Tipping points are sudden transitions in complex nonlinear systems that present unique challenges for theory and empirical work. This Review emphasizes the role of timescales, spatial complexity and complexity of ecological interactions, outlining theoretical progress that applies to these systems and providing empirical examples.

title: Levitodynamics beyond the ground state of motion
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-00997-8

Ground-state cooling of levitated particles has brought the field of levitodynamics into the quantum regime, but the next steps are less clear. This Perspective highlights advances and challenges in two key frontiers — precision sensing and generation of non-classical states of motion.

title: Getting above the clouds
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-01006-8

Paul Bate has gone from particle physics to Number 10 Downing Street to the UK Space Agency and beyond. Throughout, he has delivered on big ideas by recognizing expertise in others.

title: Meeting report: supermassive black holes and blue notes
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-01005-9

To understand the physics of supermassive black holes across cosmic time, researchers with a variety of backgrounds convened in Montréal, Canada, to find synergies across multiple length scales, wavelengths and methodologies.

title: Excitonic order in quantum materials
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-00986-x

Excitonic insulators are many-body states in which electron–hole pairing drives insulating behaviour with coherent condensate properties. This Review examines diverse experimental fingerprints of the excitonic state and proposes strategies to disentangle excitonic order from competing phases.
